content.stem: In the figure, O is the centre of the circle, and A, B and C are points on the circle with C on the major arc AB. Given that \(\angle AOB = 110^\circ\), find \(\angle ACB\). Give a reason for your answer.

diagrams.alt: A circle with centre O. Points A and B lie on the lower part of the circle and C lies at the top. Radii OA and OB are drawn, with angle AOB marked 110 degrees. Chords CA and CB are drawn, and angle ACB is marked with a question mark.

hints: How is the angle at the centre related to the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc?

solution.modelAnswer: \(\angle ACB = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle AOB = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 110^\circ = 55^\circ\), because the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle it subtends at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

steps.title: Identify the arc
steps.explanation: Both \(\angle AOB\) and \(\angle ACB\) stand on the same arc AB. \(\angle AOB\) is at the centre and \(\angle ACB\) is at the circumference, on the major arc.
steps.reason: Recognising which angles stand on the same arc tells us which theorem applies.

steps.title: Apply the theorem
steps.explanation: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc.
steps.rule: Angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference on the same arc.

steps.title: Calculate
steps.explanation: Divide the angle at the centre by 2.

commonMistakes: Doubling instead of halving: writing \(\angle ACB = 220^\circ\).
Giving the answer without stating the reason, which loses the reasoning mark.

criteria.description: States or correctly uses the relationship between the angle at the centre and the angle at the circumference
criteria.expectedEvidence: A reason such as 'angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference on the same arc', or the equation ∠AOB = 2∠ACB
acceptedAlternatives: Angle subtended at centre is double the angle subtended at the remaining part of the circle
commonErrors: Uses angles in the same segment instead

criteria.partialCreditRules: Award if the working shows halving even if the final arithmetic slips.
